messages:
incidents-bot: Paging: Elevated 5xx rate observed from private VPC egress gateway (us-west-2). Alerting threshold breached: 5xx > 4% over 3m for inference-gateway-private-prod. @oncall dings.

sara.k: seeing spikes in gateway 502/504s, started ~03:12. Customer-facing errors for a handful of Dedicated customers. :rotating_light:

mike: confirming. logs show a bunch of TCP resets to 10.2.0.0/16 peer IPs and NAT ephemeral port exhaustion on nattracker-02.

darshan.oncall: taking this. quick check: are we seeing SG denies or conntrack hits? I can be on call for next 30.

eva-network: initial glance from VPC flow logs: many SYNs then RST from transit-appliance. Also a pattern of SNAT port reuse warnings in the NAT metric stream.

kevin-sre: adding context — we rolled a transit peering route policy yesterday (policy id rp-2b) that rewrites source for egress to transit-appliance. Could be correlated.

sara.k: customer impact: ~8 Dedicated tenants showing increased 5xx and timeouts, some requests time out after 10s. CS already pinged by a customer. tagging @alex-support to coordinate comms.

alex-support: notified the affected customers, told them we're investigating and will share ETA. No broad public statement yet.

darshan.oncall: running quick checks. `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` on nattracker-02 shows 98% of conntrack table used. ephemeral port util at 98% too. Looks like conntrack + SNAT port depletion.

darshan.oncall: mitigation idea #1: temporarily increase conntrack table and ephemeral port range on nattracker-02 and nattracker-03. That'd buy time while we find root cause.

mike: second mitigation: route a subset of tenant traffic out via public-egress-gateway-01 (no transit appliance) as failover to reduce load on transit nat.

eva-network: we can program an emergency route for the /24 prefixes for impacted tenants to public-egress via BGP community tag. Need approval and 2min to push.

kevin-sre: recommended order: 1) emergency route for impacted tenants -> immediate traffic shift. 2) increase conntrack + ports. 3) dig into policy rp-2b and transit appliance logs.

sara.k: agree. we should avoid mass rolling changes. small subset first, watch metrics.

darshan.oncall: executing step 2 first (local config) since it's fastest. Running:
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="1024 65535"
```

darshan.oncall: applied on nattracker-02 and nattracker-03. conntrack usage drops from 98% -> 72% within ~30s.

ops-bot: deploy job completed: emergency-sysctl-patch applied to nattracker pool (2 nodes).

eva-network: prepping emergency route change now. I'll tag @mike for BGP session push and @kevin-sre for monitoring.

mike: pushing route for affected-tenants /24 -> public-egress-gw via bgp update (community 0xface:100). Command:
```
bgpctl inject route 10.240.88.0/24 next-hop public-egress-gw-01 community 0xface:100
```

mike: route injected for two impacted tenant prefixes. Traffic shift observed at 03:18. 5xx rate for those tenants dropped to baseline within 40s.

sara.k: good. reduced customer errors for the routed tenants. Others still showing intermittent 502s.

kevin-sre: digging into transit appliance logs: I see a steady increase in half-open connections for tenant backend peering sessions. Also see evidence of a misbehaving long-lived client holding many NAT mappings — possibly a bulk telemetry job.

darshan.oncall: can we identify source of heavy connections? netstat with PID mapping shows process id mapped to a NAT proxy in tenant infra (ten-42). Reached out to infra lead for that tenant.

eva-network: we also noticed an SG rule that was recently changed: sg-frontend-allow-all was tightened yesterday to deny egress on port range 32768-61000 for several zones, which unintentionally forced traffic through transit nat path causing port churn. That is likely contributing.

mike: so combination: policy rp-2b + tightened SG caused unexpected de-dup/rewrites -> connection churn -> conntrack exhaustion.

sara.k: action items so far: 1) we increased conntrack+port range (temp). 2) emergency route for impacted tenants (partial). 3) reached out to tenant infra for high-conn client. 4) revert SG tightening for affected zones.

kevin-sre: I'll open a config rollback PR for the SG change and get it approved as hotfix. tagging @eva-network to confirm safety.

eva-network: SG rollback approved for emergency window. Rolling back rule in zone A and B now.

eva-network: SG rule rollback completed at 03:28. Observed further drop in conntrack usage and fewer resets.

ops-bot: monitor alerts: 5xx rate for inference-gateway-private-prod reduced from 6.8% -> 1.1% over 10m. Latency p95 back to baseline.

sara.k: customer impact update: CS notified customers A/B/C that we routed their traffic and rolled back the SG rule (they reported improved success rates). No data exposure.

alex-support: prepared a short incident ack note for affected customers with ETA for full postmortem.

darshan.oncall: I'm going to hand off to @kevin-sre for longer-term remediation. I'll stay available on the thread for 30 more.

kevin-sre: taking over. next steps: 1) implement a permanent increase to conntrack and monitor, 2) add rate-based SNAT scaling (auto-allocate additional nat nodes), 3) audit rp-2b policy interactions and add guards, 4) add an alert for SG changes that affect ephemeral port ranges.

kevin-sre: creating Jira INC-1943 for follow-ups and will assign to network infra and security.

sara.k: thanks team. tagging stakeholders: @product-security, @platform-ops. Please loop in anyone for customer follow-up.

ops-bot: ticket INC-1943 created and linked: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-1943

kevin-sre: summary for handoff: root cause is combined: SNAT/conntrack saturation driven by unexpected long-lived client connections + recently tightened SG combined with routing policy rp-2b. Mitigations applied: sysctl and port range increase, route-based failover for impacted tenants, SG rollback. Impact: transient 5xx/timeouts for a small subset of Dedicated customers, now reduced to baseline. No data loss.

darshan.oncall: final note before stepping off: if pager fires again, escalate to network on-call and mark incident priority P1.

sara.k: resolving paging mute, will follow-up with postmortem draft and timeline within 48h. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: Incident resolved: 5xx rate normalized. Participants please add any leftover notes to INC-1943.
